key_insight: AEAPTMS passivation makes perovskite surface electrostatics more uniform, increases light-induced surface photovoltage, and speeds stabilization, indicating a more stable carrier landscape.
engineering_relevance: This suggests amino-silane passivation can reduce grain-boundary barriers and photovoltage losses, which is directly useful for improving perovskite solar-cell efficiency and operational stability.
method: Amplitude-modulated Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) measured dark contact potential difference (CPD) and illuminated surface photovoltage (SPV).
Compared passivated vs unpassivated mixed-cation, mixed-halide perovskite thin films at grain-boundary and grain-interior regions.
Used wavelength-dependent SPV to probe sub-bandgap electronic disorder.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports CPD distribution narrowing from about 45.7 to 14.6 mV, SPV rising from about 345 to 417 mV, and stabilization time dropping from about 840 to 470 s after AEAPTMS treatment.
watch_item: The conclusions are based on thin-film nanoscale measurements, so the device-level impact and durability under real operating conditions still need confirmation.
paper_title: Understanding surface potential dynamics of passivated perovskites via Kelvin Probe Force Microscopy
